Repo: C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Windows paths, Git-Bash/PowerShell environment). Kodely, an AI website builder. No new npm dependencies allowed.

CONTEXT — a research audit just found this exact bug, confirmed by direct grep/read, don't re-derive it, just read the cited files and fix it:
- lib/agent.ts's multi-page section (~lines 51-57) is genuinely well-built: a real router (`src/router.tsx`), a real page table (`src/pages.tsx`), per-page `.html` shells with their own SEO, `vite.config.ts` auto-discovering pages by scanning for `.html` files. This works end-to-end and is tested (tests/site-seo.test.mjs).
- BUT: `lib/templates.ts`'s own top-of-file doc comment states every one of its ~23 templates is written to satisfy "no second page," and every single template's prompt literally opens with "Build a one-page website for..." — read the file and confirm this yourself.
- `lib/wizard.ts`'s generic skeleton / `openingLine()` function hardcodes "Build a one-page website for [name] — <description>." as the FIRST sentence sent to the model on every wizard-assembled build, regardless of what the customer actually typed in their own free-text description.
- Neither `components/wizard/InlineWizard.tsx` nor `components/templates/TemplatePickerModal.tsx` has any stage, toggle, or field for page count/structure — a customer who explicitly asks for multiple pages in their own words gets that request appended AFTER an instruction that already told the model to build one page, actively contradicting them.
- Separately, a smaller real gap: lib/agent.ts's multi-page guidance explains how to ADD a page in detail (3-file recipe: page component, pages.tsx entry, .html shell) but has NO analogous guidance for REMOVING one — there's no code-level consistency check either, so a model that forgets to delete one of the three files during an edit turn can leave either an orphaned indexed page (still built, still in sitemap, invisible in nav) or a dead nav link (404).

YOUR JOB — two parts, keep them clearly separated in your work:

## Part 1: stop the wizard/templates from contradicting the customer

The goal is NOT to force every build into being multi-page — most small businesses genuinely are better served by one good page, and lib/agent.ts's own judgment guidance ("use pages when the content genuinely differs... don't manufacture thin pages to look bigger") should stay intact and in charge of that decision. The bug is narrower and more specific: the WIZARD AND TEMPLATES ACTIVELY ASSERT "one-page" as a hardcoded fact before the model even sees what the customer wants, which both overrides customer intent when they DO ask for multiple pages, and denies the model the judgment call lib/agent.ts otherwise wants it to make.

Fix:
1. In `lib/wizard.ts`: find the exact hardcoded "Build a one-page website for..." opening line construction (`openingLine()` or wherever it lives) and change it so it no longer asserts a page count — describe what's being built (the business/description) without prescribing one page vs. many. Let the model's own judgment (per lib/agent.ts's existing "use pages when content genuinely differs" guidance) decide, informed by whatever the customer's own words in the wizard's free-text fields actually say. Read the full wizard assembly flow (`assemblePrompt()` and everything that feeds it) before changing anything, so you don't break the six `LOOK_DIRECTIONS`-driven prose or any other part of the assembled prompt.
2. In `lib/templates.ts`: read the full file and its top-of-file doc comment. For each of the ~23 templates, decide on a per-template basis (don't blanket-find-replace) whether "one-page" is a genuine, deliberate constraint for that specific template's kind of business (e.g., a simple one-off landing page template MIGHT genuinely be better as one page always) or whether it's just inherited boilerplate that should instead let the model judge based on the template's actual content and whatever the customer added on top. Update the top-of-file doc comment to accurately describe the new, non-blanket approach. Do not silently turn every template into "always multi-page" either — the fix is removing an incorrect blanket assertion, not replacing it with the opposite blanket assertion.
3. Confirm (by reading, don't guess) whether `components/wizard/InlineWizard.tsx` or `components/templates/TemplatePickerModal.tsx` themselves construct or display any "one-page" framing in their own UI copy (separate from the prompt text lib/wizard.ts/lib/templates.ts assemble) — if so, fix that copy too so the UI doesn't promise/imply something the backend no longer hardcodes.
4. Do NOT add a new UI control for "how many pages" / "which pages" in this pass — that's future scope, not part of this fix. The fix is purely: stop actively asserting "one page" when nothing in the actual customer input asked for that constraint, and let the model's existing judgment guidance in lib/agent.ts do its job.

## Part 2: close the page-removal gap

1. In lib/agent.ts's multi-page section, add explicit guidance for REMOVING a page, parallel in rigor to the existing page-ADDING recipe: when a page is genuinely no longer wanted (an edit turn removes it), the model must delete all three things — the page component file, the `pages.tsx` table entry, AND the `.html` shell at project root — and explain briefly why missing any one of the three leaves either an orphaned indexed page (the `.html` shell alone keeps it building and in the sitemap even with no nav entry) or a dead nav link (a `pages.tsx`/`SiteNav` entry pointing at a deleted `.html` file 404s, since routing is real per-document navigation, not an SPA catch-all).
2. Consider (use your judgment after reading the actual generation route) whether a lightweight, genuinely useful server-side consistency check is realistically addable in this pass without over-scoping: e.g., after an edit turn's writes are applied and before/during the build step, checking whether `src/pages.tsx`'s table and the set of `.html` shells at project root agree (same set of paths) and surfacing a clear warning (not a build failure — a warning surfaced to the customer, since this is a real edit-turn code-quality signal like an existing repair/warning mechanism might already exist for). Read app/api/generate/route.ts's existing write/build/repair flow fully first to see if there's already a natural hook point (e.g., alongside however a failed-compile repair pass already works) — if adding this cleanly fits in that same pass at low risk, do it; if it would require meaningfully restructuring the generation route, leave it as a documented follow-up in your report instead of forcing it in.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Do not touch anything related to the font/design-plan work (already done, separate agent) — if you see it in lib/agent.ts, leave it as-is, just add your page-removal guidance as its own clearly-separated addition.
- Do not touch lib/features.ts, the SiteRecord/accounts backend work, or anything outside the files named above.
- Keep every template's REAL, already-good copy/business-specificity intact — you're only touching the page-count framing, not rewriting template content.

STEPS:
1. Read lib/wizard.ts, lib/templates.ts, lib/agent.ts's multi-page section, components/wizard/InlineWizard.tsx, components/templates/TemplatePickerModal.tsx, and app/api/generate/route.ts's write/build flow, fully, before changing anything.
2. Implement Part 1.
3. Implement Part 2 (guidance always; the consistency check only if it fits cleanly).
4. Run `cd /c/Users/edmem/kodely-prod && npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0` — both must be completely clean before you finish.

Report back: exactly what changed in lib/wizard.ts's opening-line construction, which templates (if any) kept a deliberate one-page constraint and why, what you added to lib/agent.ts for page removal, and whether you added the consistency check or left it as a follow-up (and why).
